claims.claim: Poincare near-extremality plus only the displayed field, energy, Sylvester, and commutator hypotheses implies a cap-independent scale-integrated MI bound.
claims.evidence: The rate-2 Laplace law eta(dy)=exp(-2|y|)dy has P(eta)=1. With smooth psi=0 on y<=0 and psi(y)=y-c on y>=2, set a_j=1-1/j, c_j=(E exp(2 a_j psi))^(-1/2), R_j=[c_j exp(a_j psi)], and Hhat_j=[a_j psi']. Then E tr R_j^2=1, E|D R_j|^2->1, the Sylvester equation holds exactly, and all commutators vanish. X_j=R_j(Y)^2 has Pareto tail exponent beta_j=1/a_j->1 and E[X_j 1_{X_j>=K}]->1 for every fixed K. Binary output-event tests yield, for h0<H<=L, liminf_j integral I(Y;Z_T)dT/T^2 >= (p0/8) log(H/h0), where p0=P(|G|>=sqrt(2))>0. Taking H=L/2 disproves a universal bound independent of L. A smooth strengthened example uses eta_delta=Law((Laplace(rate 2)+N(0,delta))/sqrt(p_delta)), where p_delta is its exact best Poincare constant; tensorization and convergence of compact-test quotients prove p_delta->1, so the rescaled law has P=1 exactly. Explicit convolution tail bounds preserve size-biased tail escape and the reciprocal tail envelope, giving the same MI lower bound without exact Pareto tails.
claims.qualification: This refutes the abstract replacement using only (7.1)-(7.2), not a stronger lemma imposing full provenance from the critical eigenfunction/tensor hierarchy. Smoothness is also met by the convolution-rescaled sequence; it still does not satisfy the source near-unit LSI provenance.

claims.claim: A reciprocal upper tail P(X_j>u)<=1/u for u>=1 together with size-biased tail escape E[X_j 1_{X_j>=K}]->1 for every fixed K forces a cap-growing scale-integrated MI lower bound in the scalar covariance Gaussian channel.
claims.evidence: For each fixed h0<H<=L and x>=H exp(H/4), set T=h/x and A_h={|Z|>=sqrt(h)}. The conditional event probability is at least p0=P(|G|>=sqrt(2)); the marginal probability is at most 3 exp(-h/4). Binary data processing gives conditional KL >= p0 h/8 for h>=h0. Integrating dT/T^2=x dh/h^2 yields liminf_j J_j(L)>= (p0/8) log(H/h0). The proof uses no Pareto asymptotics.
claims.qualification: Quantifiers are fixed L,H before j->infinity; choose H=L/2 only after that limit.

claims.claim: The smooth scalar tail field cannot be completed to the Family 093 Proposition 5.1 hierarchy by simply taking the natural eigenfield w_j proportional to R_j and rescaling its amplitude.
claims.evidence: Condition (5.2) forces I_j=E w_j^2->0 in one dimension: if I_j stays bounded below, some fixed c makes the identity rank-one projection admissible and it captures all the w_j energy. Then (5.3) has rank bound C_epsilon I_j<1, so its projection is zero and requires E b_j^2<=epsilon. At fixed s=1/8, the source decomposition gives b_j=y+s Dlog eta_j-s omega_j. On 1<=y<=2, Dlog eta_j->-2 and omega_j=w_j (or 0) tends to zero after the forced amplitude rescaling; hence b_j->y-1/4 and eta_j([1,2]) tends to positive Laplace mass, so E b_j^2 is bounded below. The smooth test does have an approximate eigenfield and its tail prediction calculation gives m_j(r)->e^-r, but this projection/outlier pair blocks the natural 1D hierarchy attempt.
claims.qualification: This is a one-dimensional candidate-specific obstruction; it does not rule out a higher-dimensional realization with diffuse w and source-generated b fields.

claims.claim: A normalized field with size-biased tail escape at every fixed threshold cannot satisfy Family 093 Proposition 3.9/7.2 near-unit LSI provenance when its derivative energy tends to one.
claims.evidence: For X_j=R_j^2 with EX_j=1 and E[X_j 1_{X_j>=K}]->1, Ent(X_j)>=log(K) E[X_j 1_{X_j>=K}]-1/e. Letting j->infinity and then K arbitrarily large forces Ent(X_j)->infinity. Source LSI instead gives Ent(R_j^2)<=2 RLSI(eta_j) E|DR_j|^2<=2 lambda_j^(-1) E|DR_j|^2->2. For matrix fields apply LSI to ||R_j||HS/sqrt(E tr(R_j^2)). The smooth scalar candidate also misses Proposition 5.1 conditions (5.2)-(5.3) under any rescaling of its natural one-dimensional eigenfield.
claims.qualification: This excludes the tail-escape falsifier from full source provenance; it does not prove the covariance-only replacement for other source-generated fields.

claims.evidence: The counterexample is not shown to arise from the source's §§5-6 eigenfunction/tensor hierarchy. The displayed hypotheses alone are insufficient, so any proof must use further structure or any corrected theorem must state it explicitly. limits: The direct rate-2 Laplace model and its smooth Gaussian-convolution/rescaling version refute only the displayed Poincare-plus-field interface, not Family 093 Proposition 7.2 with its LSI assumption.

The smooth variant has exact best Poincare constant 1 by rescaling with p_delta=P(Laplace(rate 2)*N(0,delta)); p_delta<=1+delta by tensorization and liminf p_delta>=1 by convergence of each compact smooth test quotient.
Tail escape conflicts with the near-unit LSI through diverging Ent(tr R^2); hence this counterexample cannot be realized from the full Proposition 3.9 critical sequence.

We did not verify every Proposition 5.1 prediction, projection, drift, and covariance hypothesis for the smooth test fields, construct their tensor hierarchy, or establish Proposition 6.8 frozen-matrix approximation.
No external review, formal proof checker, or numerical experiment was used.

The natural one-dimensional candidate satisfies a near-eigenfield calculation and the tail Gaussian prediction exponent, but is not a source hierarchy: conditions (5.2)-(5.3) block its amplitude-rescaled 1D realization, while Proposition 3.9 near-unit LSI excludes all such size-biased tail escape.
